assign.request: Three findings from today's studies: (1) ext/toc invisible on all 23 call sites - fix or declare dead, (2) app.js built-in top nav hidden on all 11 real destinations - delete or leave, (3) three files still gate editor controls with their own socket check instead of edit() - convert to edit()
steps: read overlap-study findings + ext/toc + approved docs three-region shape
toc: decide show vs dead, build the chosen path, verify headless at 1920 across 23 sites
toc: check overlap with related-sidebar aside at 70em on a page with both
app.js nav: read code + hiding CSS, decide delete vs leave, verify headless
edit-mode: convert the three gate lines to edit(), verify zero controls/errors at 1280 with edit off

assign.now: toc: decided show vs dead, built the fix, verifying headless

log.msg: decision: ext/toc's :not(.standard) selector excluded almost every real page (Page.class.js makes .standard the default unless classes: is set, and nothing current sets it) - this is why all 23 call sites drew nothing. Chose SHOW over DEAD: the approved docs-three-region layout (/layouts/doc/studies/approved/) names a toc rail as one of the site's five locked-in shapes for a long article. Fix: dropped :not(.standard) entirely, relying on specificity - .pages > .page:has(> .toc) is (0,3,0), already beats the base .page rule's (0,1,0), the same reason core/Page's new .page:has(> .page-related) rule (landed same day) needs no guard either. rule: code#3 (fewer, more general rules over enumerated exceptions once specificity already resolves the conflict). alternative (declare dead) and the full record written into ext/toc/doc/decisions.md.

verified headless (port 8142, 1920px): 8 of 15 real direct toc() call sites now draw a rail (core/, faq/, start/, styles/layers/base+theme+util, styles/, versus/ - all plain Pages). The other 7 (core/App, core/Router, core/Sidebar, ext/demo, ext/markdown, ext/toc itself, util/markup) are ext/Doc pages whose tabbed shell nests toc()'s output one level deeper than .pages > .page:has(> .toc) can reach - a separate, pre-existing, already-documented ext/Doc limitation, confirmed today to hit ALL 7 Doc callers not just the two overview: cases the doc used to name. Outside this task's fence (ext/Doc, not ext/toc).

correction: the brief's 'fewer than three headings draws none' does not match toc.js's actual code - fill() only removes itself at exactly zero headings (!headings.length). Verified empirically: /framework/core/ has 2 headings indexed and drew a rail anyway. Written into readme.md and decisions.md so it is not re-derived as a rule that was never real.

related-sidebar overlap check: no real page has both related: and toc() yet, so checked synthetically on /framework/versus/ (a confirmed-passing plain page) by injecting real related_aside() markup via page.evaluate at 1920, no source file touched. Result: no visual overlap - toc's higher specificity (0,3,0) wins outright over .page-related's (0,2,0), so .page-related's grid-column: related resolves to nothing and it falls back to the main column, stacked after the last content block - the same 'folds under' behaviour Page.css already documents below its own 70em breakpoint, just triggered here by a lost specificity fight instead of a narrow viewport. No page hits this today; recorded in ext/toc/doc/decisions.md for whoever builds the first page with both.

assign.now: app.js nav: confirmed dead unconditionally, deleted, verifying headless

log.msg: decision: app.js's built-in top nav is not just hidden on 11 sidebar-bearing sections (the overlap-study's framing) - it is structurally impossible for it to ever show, on any page, because Router's load_segments() always starts from app.root (public/page.js), and root itself carries classes: 'page-homepage hides-nav'. Root is a structural ancestor of every url by construction, so .app:has(.page.hides-nav.active-ancestor) matches unconditionally, site-wide. Verified headless across 14 real destinations (the 8 in app.js's own nav array plus /notes/, /imagine/, /layouts/, /websites/, /resume/, /blog/) at 1920: .nav computed display:none on every single one, no exception - including /notes/, which a same-day study file (styles/system/studies/vocabulary/tags.js) claimed was 'one of the few real destinations where the site's own top .nav actually shows' - that claim is stale/wrong as of today's live behaviour, left uncorrected since that file is outside this task's fence.

deleted: app.js's nav array + this.$nav construction (23 lines) and styles.css's .nav container rule + the whole hides-nav/--nav-display mechanism (41 lines removed, 17 added as a replacement comment). Kept .nav-link's three colour rules (3 lines) - /framework/styles/elements/text/ still demonstrates that class live as one of three named link styles (page-link/nav-link/tab) beside real prose, so deleting it would break that documentation demo; verified its swatch still renders correctly (and correctly picks up .active/.in-path colour via Router.mark_links(), since that demo page lives under /framework/). Still references the now-inert hides-nav class name/idiom for their OWN local nav-hiding, unaffected (harmless, no-op): imagine/paging/navigation/screen.js, imagine/paging/templates/families.js, layouts/labs/blogx/Blog.js+blogx.css, layouts/labs/shells/Shell.js+Shell.css. public/michael/branding/page.js:20 calls app.nav() (a method that was never defined - confirmed pre-existing, unrelated to this deletion) and throws the same error before and after my change - not a regression.

assign.now: edit-mode conversion: json.js and importance.js converted, lists verified clean, proving headless

log.msg: converted the gate line in public/imagine/cms/json/json.js:177 and public/imagine/importance/importance.js:113, both writable(){ return !Socket.singleton().disabled; } -> writable(){ return edit(); }, importing { edit } from /framework/ext/Ask/edit.js (same absolute-path pattern already used by imagine/paging/make/made.js, real.js and layouts/browse/verdicts.js). Socket import kept in both - still used for the actual rpc write/append calls.

the third named dir, public/framework/styles/system/studies/lists/, has no socket-gated editor control to convert - exhaustive grep (socket|writable|rpc|localhost|edit() across page.js/lists.css/doc/decisions.md/readme.md) found nothing but one unrelated comment ('the one writable FACT in the whole page'). The module's drag-to-reassign is a pure in-memory demo with no server write path at all (its own doc says so: 'a demo, so nothing here is saved') - confirmed at both its new location and the /imagine/design/lists/ stub left behind by today's move. Nothing to fix here; recorded as a verified finding, not a deferral.

verified headless (port 8142, 1280px), edit toggle forced off via localStorage lew42-edit:{on:false} (the same key the rail's real checkbox writes): /imagine/cms/json/edit/, /imagine/importance/, /imagine/importance/judge/, /imagine/importance/ranked/ all correctly show their existing read-only messaging and zero console/page errors. cms/json/edit/ disables 5 buttons (attr disabled, its own pre-existing read_only() behaviour, unchanged). importance's Add/judge buttons stay visible but the underlying write() still throws-and-is-caught (try/catch in views.js's add()), shown as a message, not a console error - this UI pattern (message beside an active button, vs disabling it) predates this task and was not redesigned, per the brief's 'the gate line only.' Re-verified with edit ON (default): zero errors across all four plus the lists page.

assign.outcome:
**Three dead-nav findings, all fixed and verified headless.** `ext/toc` now draws on 8 of its 15 real, direct call sites at 1920 (`:not(.standard)` deleted — it excluded almost every page); `app.js`'s built-in top nav was structurally dead on every page, not just 11 (root's own `hides-nav` is an ancestor of every url), so it's deleted outright (23 lines from `app.js`, net 24 from `styles.css`); `imagine/cms/json` and `imagine/importance` now gate their editor controls through `edit()` instead of their own socket check, proven with the rail's toggle off at 1280.

- [`ext/toc`](/framework/ext/toc/) — the fixed component, [`doc/decisions.md`](/framework/ext/toc/doc/decisions.md) has the full record (options considered, the count, a correction to the brief's own "fewer than three headings" claim, the related-sidebar overlap check)
- [`imagine/cms/json/edit/`](/imagine/cms/json/edit/) and [`imagine/importance/`](/imagine/importance/) — both converted, both verified read-only and error-free with edit off

**Left open, on purpose:** 7 of the 15 toc call sites (`core/App`, `core/Router`, `core/Sidebar`, `ext/demo`, `ext/markdown`, `ext/toc` itself, `util/markup`) are `ext/Doc` pages whose own tabbed shell nests `toc()`'s output too deep for the fix to reach — a separate, pre-existing `ext/Doc` limitation (already flagged in `ext/toc`'s own docs, now confirmed to hit every `Doc` caller, not just two) outside this task's fence. No real page has both `related:` and `toc()` yet, so their grid interaction is checked and documented but not hardened — `core/Page` is fenced off. `public/framework/styles/system/studies/lists/` had no socket gate to convert at all — verified exhaustively, not a deferral.
